We've now explored the empty states, behavior at scale, and the unusual/error situations across every part of the app, and each addition has settled cleanly. I think we've fully mapped what this first version should do.

Here's everything we've settled — in plain terms:

1. **Quick saving** — paste a link and its title, description, site icon, and (when available) a preview image are filled in for you; no duplicates.
2. **Your own touches** — edit any of those details plus the address, add a note (with light formatting), and add tags that suggest ones you've already used.
3. **Read later** — mark links to read later and see just those in one place.
4. **Finding things** — a search box that ranges from simple word searches to exact tags, phrases, and and/or/not logic; plus clicking a tag to see everything with it.
5. **Ordering** — a dropdown to sort by newest, oldest, or title, with newest first as the default.
6. **Tidying up** — archive older links out of the way (fully reversible), or permanently delete with a confirmation.
7. **Holds up when large** — one continuous, searchable list with sensible trimming of long text.
8. **Graceful with problems** — rejects junk addresses, never loses a link even if its details can't be fetched, and handles re-saving something you'd archived.
9. **Yours everywhere** — one private collection, behind a simple sign-in, that's the same on your computer and your phone.

I've also noted one thing for a **later round** (not this build): a settings screen where you pick your own default sort order.

**May I now start building this as the real application?** Once you say go, I'll switch from exploring to implementing this exact scope. (This is a deliberate hand-off point — I won't start building until you confirm.)
